description:
FOUND s455c (Fable perf review). The regexg row (added s454ac) prints 0.0012s then 0.0000s across sessions while a DIRECT run of its exact program via runpcl takes ~0.31s wall (1M matches, correct output 200000) -- so the row measures nothing: its startup-subtraction small-N run appears to do the same work as the big-N run (n=5 both?), and the subtraction cancels. NOT a product bug: rg1-rg6 probes (empty body / counting / outer topic+named loops, literal+variable ends, both PCL_OPT regimes) all ~0.30-0.35s wall; the one 2.3s outlier reproduced only as a first-run CORE REBUILD after a runtime-changing merge. FIX: make the row honest in tools/bench-exec.pl (big/small iteration counts must differ; verify by hand-timing the row program at two N). Owner: round-14 perf agent, before quoting any regexg number.
CLOSED s459am.  THE CAUSE WAS NOT THE ONE THIS TASK GUESSED, and the guess is
worth recording as wrong: the big/small counts were NOT both 5 (they were 5
and 0) and the subtraction did not "cancel" in any arithmetic sense.
MEASURED FIRST (the s335 rule): perl's side of the row was always honest and
scales linearly -- N=0 0.0025 s, N=5 0.0618, N=20 0.2397, N=100 1.1914.  PCL's
side was FLAT at 0.0389 s for every one of those N.  A program that costs the
same at N=0 and N=100 is not running, and it was not: `tools/bench-exec.pl`
hand-wrote its own SBCL command line instead of using tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm, so
it ran PCL on SBCL's 2 MB DEFAULT control stack, where the row's very first
statement -- `my $x = 'a' x 200000` -- died with `Control stack exhausted`.
`2>&1 >/dev/null` hid it, both runs crashed at the same point, and the
difference of two crashes is 0.0000 s.  This is #324 exactly: bench-exec was a
SEVENTH runner spawning SBCL, and the one that drifted.
THREE FIXES, all in s459am:
 (a) tools/bench-exec.pl takes its command line from PCLSbcl like every other
     runner (so the stack is the 512 MB every other measurement uses);
 (b) EVERY ROW IS VERIFIED BEFORE IT IS TIMED -- both engines run once at
     N_big and their stdout must match, and PCL must exit 0, or the row prints
     BROKEN and is not timed.  A crashed run is fast; without this check the
     table's most attractive number is its least trustworthy one.  This is the
     part that makes the class of bug impossible rather than fixed once;
 (c) the underlying product bug is task #880 (p-str-x's `apply` over N
     arguments) -- fixed, so the row would now survive even a small stack.
N_big raised 5 -> 30: at 5 the signal (~0.06 s of perl) sits under the
run-to-run spread of the ~1 s constant term both runs pay to compile the
program at load.  VERIFIED AT TWO N as this task required: 2.21x at N=5 and
2.19x at N=30, i.e. the row now agrees with itself.  regexg reads 2.19x where
it read 0.01x.
Residue filed as #881 (the `strcat` row has the same too-small-signal problem,
without the crash).
subject: bench-exec regexg row reads 0.0000x -- the big/small-N subtraction cancels (row broken as an instrument); direct runpcl timing of the same shape is ~0.3s wall incl. startup
